verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents internal status pages meant for the internal team only: each incident gets an ephemeral page that collects updates posted from Slack or Command Center. That covers the employee-only half of the story, but the docs say these pages need no auth or license to view for org-public incidents, so access control is thin, and the only external pages documented are public ones. Missing for 10: customer-specific private status pages, configurable access control (SSO- or password-gated audiences), persistent rather than per-incident internal pages, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering leader, I can run private or internal status pages with access control for customer-specific or employee-only audiences

citations.quote: The FireHydrant platform offers both internal status pages, which are meant for the internal team only and require no setup
For public (to your organization) incidents, these internal status pages do not require auth or a FireHydrant license to view.
each incident on FireHydrant will have a dedicated ephemeral status page that summarizes high-level details and includes key links.
